notes: First run of the plan. Keep it easy and conversational the whole way. Focus on form — short quick strides, relaxed shoulders.
warmupNote: Standard full warm-up. This sets the tone for the next 10 weeks.
cooldownNote: Standard full cool-down. Take your time — no rush after an easy run.

notes: Run 3.5 miles easy, then do 4 strides of 20 seconds at near-sprint effort with 60-sec walk recovery between each. Strides wake up fast-twitch fibres without fatiguing you.
warmupNote: Standard warm-up. Add A-skips (step 9) today since you're doing strides.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down. Pay extra attention to the quad stretch after the strides.

notes: First long run. Run by effort not pace — if a hill slows you to 11:30, that's fine. Practice your race-day nutrition routine: water every 20 min.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Spend extra time on hip circles and leg swings before a long run.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down with extra time on pigeon pose (90 sec each side) and hamstring stretch after the longer distance.

notes: True recovery run. If you're sore from last week, keep this very easy at 11:30+ /mi.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. If legs are sore, extend the brisk walk to 5 minutes before jogging.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down. Focus on the hip flexor lunge if you're feeling tightness from the weekend.

pace: Warm-up 1 mi easy | 2 × 1.5 mi at 9:30–9:45 /mi | Cool-down 1 mi
notes: First structured workout. Recovery between intervals: 3 min easy jog. Do NOT go faster than 9:30/mi — the goal is sustained effort, not sprinting.
warmupNote: Full warm-up plus A-skips. The 1-mile easy warm-up within the workout counts as additional prep.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After tempo work, spend extra time on the calf stretches (both straight and bent knee).

notes: Add one mile over last week. Stay fully conversational. Take a gel or 4 oz of sports drink at mile 3.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Hip circles and leg swings are especially important before longer runs.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down with extra time on pigeon pose and IT band stretch.

notes: Midweek flush. Keep it easy — this is recovery from the weekend, not a workout.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 are sufficient for easy days.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

pace: Warm-up 1 mi | 3.5 mi at 9:30–9:45 /mi | Cool-down 1 mi
notes: Continuous tempo this week (no breaks). If you need to drop pace, slow to 10:00/mi but keep running — no walking during the tempo block.
warmupNote: Full warm-up including A-skips. You need the neuromuscular activation before a sustained tempo.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After 3.5 miles at tempo, your calves and hip flexors will be tight — give them extra time.

notes: Biggest mileage jump yet. Break it mentally into thirds. Practice drinking on the run without stopping — you'll need this in the race.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Spend extra time on lateral lunges and ankle prep.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. Walk for 5 full minutes before stretching. Hold each stretch for the full duration — don't rush.

notes: Run each 400m (0.25 mi) at hard effort, then jog 400m easy to recover. These teach your legs what fast feels like. If paces feel too hard, aim for 8:30–8:45/mi.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Speed work requires thorough preparation — do not skip any steps today.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After intervals, your legs will be fatigued — the walk cool-down is extra important before stretching.

notes: Recovery from Wednesday's speed work. Zero pressure — just accumulate easy miles. Focus on consistent cadence (~170 steps/min).
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 only today.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

notes: First run over 5 miles. Mile 6–8 will feel new — slow down if needed but keep moving. Bring a gel and take it at mile 4.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Extra attention on hip circles and leg swings.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. 5-min walk, then full stretching sequence. Hold pigeon pose for 90 sec each side today.

pace: Warm-up 1 mi | 4 mi at 9:15–9:30 /mi | Cool-down 1 mi
notes: Biggest tempo yet. Target 9:15/mi if you're feeling strong, 9:30 if it's a tough day. This is your most important workout of the week.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Don't skip any steps — you're about to run 4 miles at a hard effort.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After 4 miles at tempo pace, give extra time to calf stretches and the IT band stretch.

notes: Pure recovery. Resist any urge to push — your legs need to absorb Wednesday's effort.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 only.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

notes: Double digits are close. Stay patient through miles 6–7, which are typically the hardest. Take nutrition at miles 3 and 6.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. This is a significant distance — thorough preparation matters.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. Walk 5 min, then full stretching sequence. Pay special attention to the quad and hip flexor stretches.

notes: More reps than Week 4. Aim for 8:00–8:15/mi. Recovery jog: 400m between each. If pace slips after rep 6, that's fine — push through the last two.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Your fastest workout paces are today — prep is non-negotiable.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After 8 intervals, your legs need serious recovery work.

pace: 1 mi easy | 4 mi at 9:00–9:09 /mi | 1 mi easy
notes: First sustained race-pace effort. This is the key workout of the block. 9:09/mi should feel hard but controlled — if it feels easy, you started too fast.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Race pace work demands your best preparation.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. The IT band and pigeon pose are especially important after race-pace efforts.

notes: First double-digit run! Major milestone. Slow down in miles 4–6 if needed — finishing strong matters more than early pace. Fuel at miles 3, 6, and 8.5.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Take your time — this is a long day.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. Walk 5+ minutes. Hold every stretch for the full duration. You earned it.

pace: Warm-up 1 mi | 4 mi at 9:10–9:20 /mi | Cool-down 1 mi
notes: Tempo at near-race pace. This is where the sub-2 hour fitness is built. The goal is to make 9:09/mi feel normal and sustainable.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. Extra attention on calf stretches (both variations) and the IT band.

notes: Flush the legs from Wednesday. Short and relaxed. Focus on breathing and form.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 only.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

notes: Second-longest run of the cycle. At this distance you're genuinely half marathon-ready. Aim for a negative split — run the second half slightly faster than the first. Fuel at miles 3, 6, and 9.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. 11 miles deserves thorough preparation.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. 5-min walk minimum. Full stretching sequence with extra time on pigeon pose, hamstrings, and hip flexors.

notes: 800m repeats are the gold standard for half marathon fitness. Run each 800m (0.5 mi) at comfortably hard effort. 90-sec jog recovery between each. This is the hardest workout of the plan.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. The hardest workout of the plan — leave nothing out.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After 5 × 800m, your legs need serious recovery. Walk for 5 full minutes before stretching.

pace: 1 mi easy | 5 mi at 9:00–9:09 /mi | 1 mi easy
notes: 5 miles at goal race pace. If you can complete this, you have the fitness for a sub-2 half. Stay relaxed in miles 2–3. Miles 4–5 will be hard — hold form.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Race pace for 5 miles requires your best preparation.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. Don't skip the spinal twist and child's pose after this effort.

notes: PEAK LONG RUN — the most important single run of the plan. This is 92% of race distance. Run conservatively: miles 1–5 should feel easy. Fuel at miles 3, 6, 9, and 11. Finishing this run is a major confidence marker.
warmupNote: Full warm-up. Take 12–15 minutes on prep today. Your body needs it.
cooldownNote: Extended cool-down. Walk 5–7 minutes. Hold every stretch for the full duration, especially pigeon pose (90 sec), hip flexors, and hamstrings.

weekFocus: Taper Begins — Volume Down, Intensity Stays
pace: Warm-up 1 mi | 3 mi at 9:10 /mi | Cool-down 1 mi
notes: Shorter tempo than peak weeks but same pace. You may feel surprisingly strong — that's the taper effect. Don't use that energy to run extra miles.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down.

weekFocus: Taper Begins — Volume Down, Intensity Stays
notes: Relaxed shakeout. Notice how much faster easy pace feels. Your body is recovering.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 only.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

weekFocus: Taper Begins — Volume Down, Intensity Stays
notes: Last long run. Treat it as a confidence run — you've done the hard work. Practice your race-day routine: shoes, socks, nutrition, gear.
warmupNote: Full warm-up.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After this run, your taper is well underway — enjoy the recovery.

weekFocus: Full Taper — Sharpen for Race Day
notes: Easy and relaxed. Your legs should start feeling bouncy and fresh. Trust the taper.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. Steps 1–8 only.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

weekFocus: Full Taper — Sharpen for Race Day
pace: 1 mi easy | 3 mi at 9:05–9:09 /mi | 1 mi easy
notes: Last workout before race week. Run exactly your race pace for 3 miles to confirm the pace feels locked in. Then shut it down — no extras.
warmupNote: Full warm-up with A-skips. Last hard effort before the race — do it right.
cooldownNote: Full cool-down. After this session, the hay is in the barn.

weekFocus: Full Taper — Sharpen for Race Day
notes: Short and gentle. Finish and feel good. You're fully primed for race week.
warmupNote: Light warm-up. 5-min walk only — no need for full dynamic prep.
cooldownNote: Standard cool-down.

weekFocus: Race Week — Stay Fresh, Stay Confident, Execute
notes: Keep legs loose. Nothing heroic — 20–25 minutes of easy jogging.
warmupNote: 5-min walk only. You're this close to the race — don't stress the legs.
cooldownNote: Light stretch: quad, calf, hip flexor, hamstring only. 5 minutes total.

weekFocus: Race Week — Stay Fresh, Stay Confident, Execute
notes: Complete rest. Walk only. Eat a larger-than-normal dinner with complex carbs (pasta, rice, sweet potato). Lay out all race gear tonight: shoes, socks, bib, watch, nutrition.
warmupNote: No run today. Gentle 5-minute walk after dinner to aid digestion.
cooldownNote: No stretching needed. Elevate your legs for 10 minutes before bed.

weekFocus: Race Week — Stay Fresh, Stay Confident, Execute
notes: Start conservatively — adrenaline will make 9:20/mi feel like a jog. Let people pass you in mile 1. Settle in at miles 4–8. If you have energy at mile 10, begin your push. Finish strong — 10 weeks of training led to this moment.
warmupNote: 15-min pre-race warm-up 30 minutes before start: 5-min walk, leg swings, hip circles, high knees, butt kicks, 3-min easy jog. Keep it short — you're about to run 13.1 miles.
cooldownNote: Post-race: walk for 10 minutes, then light stretching (quad, calf, hamstring, hip flexor). You've earned every minute of rest.
